metadata.description_blurb: Luxury rarely says dead stock out loud. High margins historically paid for overproduction to avoid stockouts — until EU rules closed the destruction exit, and AI demand forecasting became the quiet fix.

beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Komal. Luxury loves the word scarcity. It hates the word dead stock. Watch what happens when overproduction stops being an acceptable hedge — and A.I. demand forecasting becomes the quiet way out.

props.command: How is AI used to predict demand and cut overproduction in luxury — name the dead-stock problem, the old hedge, the regulatory pressure, and the forecasting fix.
output: Dead stock: made, unsold, still on the books
Old hedge: overproduce to avoid stockouts
Fix: AI forecast by style, size, geography

beats.narration_text: They call it leftover. Inventory adjustment. Markdown risk. The honest word is dead stock: goods that were made, never found a buyer at full price, and still sit on the books. Luxury does not put that word on the campaign.

Why overproduce at all? Stockouts feel worse. Empty shelf, lost sale, client walks. Bain's read: luxury's high margins let houses overlook overproduction to avoid that risk. Unsold inventory becomes the quiet tax — margin and carbon both.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Why overproduce at all? Stockouts feel worse. Empty shelf, lost sale, client walks. Bain's read: luxury's high margins let houses overlook overproduction to avoid that risk. Unsold inventory becomes the quiet tax — margin and carbon both.

beats.narration_text: The old exit ramp was destruction — burn or shred to protect exclusivity. Europe closed it. Under the Ecodesign rules, large companies cannot destroy unsold clothes, accessories, and footwear from July nineteenth, twenty twenty-six. Keep it in use, or don't make so much.

beats.narration_text: So the smarter move is upstream: predict demand before you cut. A.I. sales forecasting reads style, size, and geography — not a buyer's gut alone. Bain: roughly sixty percent of fashion brands are already using or testing it. That is the mechanism, not a sustainability slogan.

Bain: roughly sixty percent of fashion brands are already using or testing it. That is the mechanism, not a sustainability slogan.

beats.narration_text: Forecast alone is not enough. The next step is allocation: put units where demand actually is — Paris, Milan, New York — not everywhere by habit. Bain again: about half of brands already use A.I. to allocate stock more precisely. Right door. Fewer leftovers.

Here's the design tell. Theater keeps the same buy calendar and hopes the campaign sounds green. Mechanism changes the buy: forecast, allocate, smaller wrong bets. If overproduction does not fall, the A.I. story is marketing. Full stop.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Dead stock is the name luxury avoids. The old hedge was overproduce to dodge stockouts. Europe's destruction ban closed the brand-protecting exit. A.I. demand forecasting and allocation are the upstream fix — style, size, geography. Design judgment: if unsold does not fall, the model was theater.

artifactLines: Problem: dead stock — made, unsold, still on the books (luxury rarely says the word).
Old hedge: overproduce to avoid stockouts; high margins absorbed the waste (Bain).
Pressure: EU ESPR — large companies banned from destroying unsold apparel/footwear from 19 July 2026.
Fix: AI sales forecasting (~60% using/testing) + AI stock allocation (~half of brands).
The rule: if overproduction doesn't fall, the AI story is marketing.
